```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {selectControl, loadWeekData, weekIssueTimeline, mmeSkillByLead, mmeSkillMaps, mmePatterns, mmeForecastMaps, mmeScoresByLead, mmeFlexible} from "../assets/leads/leads.js"
mme = loadWeekData("../assets/pentad-mme-2023/")
geo = ({indonesia: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/indonesia.geojson").json(),
  provinces: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/provinces.geojson").json(),
  neighbours: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/neighbours.geojson").json()})
leadChoices = mme.targets.map((t, i) => [String(t.lead), `${mme.leadShort[i]}: ${t.label}`])
modelChoices = mme.models.map(m => [m, m === "MME" ? "MME (the ensemble)" : m])
memberChoices = modelChoices.filter(([m]) => m !== "MME")
```

::: {.eyebrow}
Subseasonal · Pentad rainfall · Multi-model ensemble · Full Indonesia
:::

The [single-model pentad case](pentad-leads-2023.qmd) calibrated one model, GEFSv12, for
the next six pentads. This case asks the same question of **every subseasonal model
that can answer it** and averages the calibrated forecasts into a multi-model
ensemble (MME). It shows the outputs of the
[seasonal](seasonal-mme-2023.qmd) and [monthly](monthly-mme-2023.qmd) ensembles: skill
for every member and for the ensemble, EOF patterns and CCA modes, calibrated
forecasts, and the flexible forecast.

Everything is at CHIRPS v3.0's native 0.05° grid: the 69,638 pixels that touch
Indonesia's 38-province boundary and have data in every training target. All
numbers on this page come from the [executed notebook](../notebooks/pentad-mme-2023.ipynb).
Hover, tap or use the arrow keys on any map or chart to read values; maps load when
you choose them, and the maps in a group zoom and pan together.

::: {.callout-note title="The short result"}
- **Averaging five models changes the correlation very little.** The ensemble's
  cross-validated correlation (CCA) is 0.31, 0.31, 0.25, 0.22, 0.15 and 0.14 from pentad +1 to
  pentad +6; GEFSv12 alone scores 0.31, 0.30, 0.25, 0.24, 0.17 and 0.13. It is above GEFSv12 alone at pentad +1, pentad +2 and pentad +6 and below it at pentad +4 and pentad +5, and level with it (within 0.005) at pentad +3.
- **No single model is best at every lead.** The best single member is GEFSv12 at pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5 and CCSM4 at pentad +6. By correlation the ensemble ranks first of six at pentad +1 and pentad +2, second of six at pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5 and second of five at pentad +6.
- **Without calibration, averaging helps more.** The plain average of the five
  models' raw rainfall anomalies correlates at 0.43, 0.40, 0.32, 0.27, 0.23 and 0.21, above raw
  GEFSv12 (0.42, 0.38, 0.28, 0.23, 0.17 and 0.14) and above the calibrated ensemble at
  every lead.
- **Probabilities beat a no-model forecast at every lead**: the ensemble's
  cross-validated RPSS is 0.034 to 0.086, above GEFSv12's at pentad +1, pentad +2 and pentad +6, not at pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5.
- **In November 2023 the ensemble leaned dry.** It made below normal the most likely
  category over 53 to 89% of the area. Below normal was the most widespread observed category at pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3 and pentad +4; at pentad +5 and pentad +6 it was near normal.
:::

## One issue date, five models

The targets are those of the single-model case: the next six pentads after the issue
of **31 October 2023**, observed with the CHIRPS v3.0 pentad product. Five SubX models in the IRI Data
Library have hindcasts and 2023 runs with values for them: GEFSv12, CFSv2,
GEOS_V2p1, CCSM4 and FIMr1p1. Training uses the **October-December targets of
2000-2016**, the years all five hindcast sets share. The single-model case used
2000-2018.

The models do not start on the same days, so one rule decides which run of each
answers an issue date, in training and in 2023:

- **Each model uses its latest run on or before the issue date, at most 6 days
  earlier.** The target is the same calendar days for every model, so a model that
  started earlier is used at a longer lead.
- **CFSv2** is the mean of its four six-hourly runs up to 00 UTC on the issue date.
- **Training issue dates are Wednesdays**, the only days GEFSv12's hindcasts start,
  chosen as in the single-model case (1 to 7 days before the pentad for pentad +1, 3 to 9 for +2, 8 to 14 for +3, 13 to 19 for +4, 18 to 24 for +5 and 23 to 29 for +6).

| Model | 2023 run used | Days behind the issue date | Members, 2023 | Members, training | Days behind in training (min / mean / max) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEFSv12 | 2023-10-31 00:00 | 0 | 31 | 11 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| CFSv2 | 2023-10-30 06:00 to 2023-10-31 00:00 (4 runs) | 0 | 16 | 4 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| GEOS | 2023-10-28 00:00 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 0 / 1.77 / 4 |
| CCSM4 | 2023-10-29 00:00 | 2 | 9 | 3 | 0 / 2.1 / 5 |
| FIM | 2023-10-25 00:00 | 6 | 4 | 4 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

: The run of each model that answers the issue of 31 October 2023, and the same rule across the training samples. Source: [start-rule.csv](../data/pentad-mme-2023/start-rule.csv).

Two things in this table affect how the 2023 forecasts should be read. The 2023
runs of GEFSv12, CFSv2 and CCSM4 have more members than their hindcasts, so their
2023 ensemble means are less noisy than the ones the calibration was trained on.
And a model whose run is several days old in 2023 was not always that late in
training: the last column gives the range.

FIMr1p1 forecasts 32 days. Its latest run on or before the issue date started on 2023-10-25, so it does not reach pentad +6: the ensemble has five members at pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5 and four at pentad +6.

| Pentad +2 | 6-10 Nov 2023 | 5 | none | 304 |
| Pentad +3 | 11-15 Nov 2023 | 5 | none | 303 |

## One calibration, 58 times

Each member is calibrated for each lead with **CCA** (3 predictor and 3 predictand
EOFs, 2 CCA modes) and **PCR** (3 predictor EOFs), the settings of the single-model
case, fixed before any skill was computed. Both fields are anomalies from the mean
over the training years. The cross-validation window is 35 samples: a year
holds about 18 targets per lead, so a left-out target's neighbours within about a year are
left out with it. Every member at a lead is trained on the same targets, those all
of that lead's members have a run for (300 to 305 per lead).

The fits go through `cptcore`, the layer PyCPT's `evaluate_models` calls: 58 fits
in all. At 0.05° a CCA fit took 138 to 369 minutes and a PCR fit 29 to 90 minutes, with many
running side by side.

The ensemble is built as PyCPT's `construct_mme` builds it: the **equal-weight
average** of the members' cross-validated hindcasts, deterministic forecasts,
prediction error variances and tercile probabilities. The notebook checks that
CPT's Pearson map of every member equals the correlation recomputed from its
hindcasts to within 0.00001, and that its own 2AFC function, used for the ensemble,
reproduces CPT's 2AFC map of a member to within 0.3 percentage points.

## Skill of every member, and of the ensemble

Area-weighted means over Indonesia, cross-validated over the training targets.
**Pearson correlation** is 0 for no linear relationship. **2AFC** is the chance that
the hindcasts rank two different targets in the observed order, 50% for no skill
[(Mason and Weigel 2009)](https://doi.org/10.1175/2008MWR2553.1).

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof chartMethod = selectControl("Calibration", ["CCA", "PCR"], "CCA")
viewof chartMetric = selectControl("Score", [["Pearson", "Pearson correlation"], ["2AFC (%)", "2AFC"], ["CV RPSS", "Cross-validated RPSS"]], "Pearson")
mmeSkillByLead(mme, chartMethod, chartMetric)
```
:::

| Lead | Target | Members | MME | GEFSv12 alone | Best member | Raw multi-model mean | Raw GEFSv12 | Pixels where MME beats GEFSv12 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Pentad +2 | 6-10 Nov 2023 | 5 | 0.31 | 0.30 | GEFSv12, 0.30 | 0.40 | 0.38 | 61% |
| Pentad +3 | 11-15 Nov 2023 | 5 | 0.25 | 0.25 | GEFSv12, 0.25 | 0.32 | 0.28 | 47% |
| Pentad +4 | 16-20 Nov 2023 | 5 | 0.22 | 0.24 | GEFSv12, 0.24 | 0.27 | 0.23 | 33% |
| Pentad +5 | 21-25 Nov 2023 | 5 | 0.15 | 0.17 | GEFSv12, 0.17 | 0.23 | 0.17 | 32% |
| Pentad +6 | 26-30 Nov 2023 | 4 | 0.14 | 0.13 | CCSM4, 0.15 | 0.21 | 0.14 | 70% |

: Pearson correlation of the CCA calibrations, area-weighted mean over 69,638 pixels, cross-validated over the October-December targets of 2000-2016. Source: [mme-against-members.csv](../data/pentad-mme-2023/mme-against-members.csv).

Read across a row. It is above GEFSv12 alone at pentad +1, pentad +2 and pentad +6 and below it at pentad +4 and pentad +5, and level with it (within 0.005) at pentad +3. The best single member is GEFSv12 at pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5 and CCSM4 at pentad +6, and the
ensemble ranks first of six at pentad +1 and pentad +2, second of six at pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5 and second of five at pentad +6. With PCR the ensemble scores
0.32, 0.32, 0.26, 0.22, 0.16 and 0.15.

GEFSv12 alone scores 0.31, 0.30, 0.25, 0.24, 0.17 and 0.13 here. In the single-model case,
trained on 2000-2018, its CCA correlation was 0.30, 0.30, 0.25, 0.23, 0.18 and 0.13: the two
agree to within 0.01 although the training years and samples differ.

The two raw columns involve no fitting. Averaging the five models' raw anomalies
lifts the correlation above raw GEFSv12 at every lead, by 0.01 to 0.07. The
calibrated ensemble is below the raw average at every lead, by 0.06 to 0.12. Two
things should be kept in mind. The raw correlations do not carry the downward bias
of cross-validation described below. And the raw average is not a forecast
product: it has model biases and no probabilities. This page does not establish why
calibration through three EOFs keeps less of the gain from averaging.


### Probabilities, cross-validated

PyCPT's own probabilistic scores are computed from in-sample probabilities, so they
are not used here. The notebook builds cross-validated tercile probabilities
instead. For each training year it leaves out **every target of that year**, takes
the tercile boundaries from the remaining observations and the error spread from
the remaining cross-validated errors, and gives each left-out target a Student's t
distribution centred on its cross-validated hindcast. The ranked probability skill
score (**RPSS**) compares those probabilities with a forecast with **no model** put
through the same steps: for a target, the mean of the other years' anomalies. Above
0 means the model adds information. This construction is this tutorial's, not
CPT's.

| Lead | Target | MME | GEFSv12 alone | Highest member |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pentad +1 | 1-5 Nov 2023 | 0.086 | 0.085 | GEFSv12, 0.085 |
| Pentad +2 | 6-10 Nov 2023 | 0.081 | 0.078 | GEFSv12, 0.078 |
| Pentad +3 | 11-15 Nov 2023 | 0.061 | 0.061 | GEFSv12, 0.061 |
| Pentad +4 | 16-20 Nov 2023 | 0.051 | 0.058 | GEFSv12, 0.058 |
| Pentad +5 | 21-25 Nov 2023 | 0.034 | 0.038 | GEFSv12, 0.038 |
| Pentad +6 | 26-30 Nov 2023 | 0.035 | 0.030 | CCSM4, 0.032 |

: Cross-validated RPSS of the CCA calibrations against a no-model forecast put through the same steps, area-weighted mean. Source: [skill-by-lead.csv](../data/pentad-mme-2023/skill-by-lead.csv).

The ensemble's RPSS is positive at every lead and above GEFSv12's at pentad +1, pentad +2 and pentad +6, not at pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5. By this score it
ranks first of six at pentad +1, pentad +2 and pentad +3, second of six at pentad +4 and pentad +5 and first of five at pentad +6.

The ensemble's correlation when one member is left out. A value above the full
ensemble's means the ensemble is better without that model.

| Lead | All members | Without GEFSv12 | Without CFSv2 | Without GEOS | Without CCSM4 | Without FIM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pentad +1 | 0.313 | 0.306 | 0.305 | 0.316 | 0.314 | 0.314 |
| Pentad +2 | 0.306 | 0.297 | 0.299 | 0.307 | 0.307 | 0.307 |
| Pentad +3 | 0.249 | 0.230 | 0.246 | 0.250 | 0.248 | 0.252 |
| Pentad +4 | 0.215 | 0.189 | 0.218 | 0.222 | 0.214 | 0.217 |
| Pentad +5 | 0.146 | 0.121 | 0.149 | 0.156 | 0.136 | 0.155 |
| Pentad +6 | 0.141 | 0.138 | 0.139 | 0.148 | 0.126 | not a member |

: Cross-validated correlation of the CCA ensemble with one member left out, area-weighted mean. Source: [leave-one-out.csv](../data/pentad-mme-2023/leave-one-out.csv).

The member whose removal costs the most is CFSv2 at pentad +1, GEFSv12 at pentad +2, pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +5 and CCSM4 at pentad +6 (a change of -0.008, -0.010, -0.019, -0.026, -0.025 and -0.015 by lead).
Removing a model raises the correlation in some cases: GEOS, CCSM4 and FIM at pentad +1; GEOS and CCSM4 at pentad +2; GEOS and FIM at pentad +3; CFSv2, GEOS and FIM at pentad +4; CFSv2, GEOS and FIM at pentad +5; GEOS at pentad +6. Each of those changes is at most 0.010.
These are area means of one training period; the table does not show that any
model should be dropped.

### Why a correlation near zero is not "no skill" here

Cross-validation biases correlation downward. The forecast with **no model at all**,
the mean of the other years, correlates *negatively* with the observations: leaving
a wet target out lowers the mean of the rest. The notebook measures it: the
no-model forecast has an area-mean correlation of -0.37 at these leads
[(Barnston and van den Dool 1993)](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(1993)006%3C0963:ADICVS%3E2.0.CO;2).
A calibrated model's correlation is not simply shifted by that amount, which is why
this page compares correlations with each other and reads them alongside the RPSS,
whose reference is that same no-model forecast.

### Where the skill is

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mapModel = selectControl("Model", modelChoices, "MME")
viewof mapMethod = selectControl("Calibration", [["CCA", "CCA"], ["PCR", "PCR"], ["raw", "None (raw model)"]], "CCA")
viewof mapMetric = selectControl("Score", [["pearson", "Pearson correlation"], ["rpss", "Cross-validated RPSS"]], "pearson")
mmeSkillMaps(mme, geo, mapModel, mapMethod, mapMetric)
```
:::

## EOF patterns and CCA modes

CCA does not relate the two fields pixel by pixel. It first reduces each to a few
**EOFs**, patterns that explain the most variance from target to target, each with
a score per target. It then finds pairs of combinations of those, the **CCA modes**,
whose score series are as correlated as possible.

Choose a model, a lead and a mode. The top map is the pattern in the model's
rainfall over the predictor box, the second the pattern in observed rainfall over
Indonesia, and the chart their scores at each training target.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof patModel = selectControl("Model", memberChoices, "GEFSv12")
viewof patLead = selectControl("Lead", leadChoices, "1")
viewof patKind = selectControl("Show", [["cca", "CCA mode"], ["eof", "EOF"]], "cca")
viewof patMode = selectControl("Mode", [["1", "1"], ["2", "2"], ["3", "3 (EOF only)"]], "1")
mmePatterns(mme, geo, patLead, patModel, patKind, patMode)
```
:::

How to read them, and how not to:

- The patterns come from the fit to **all training targets**, not from the
  cross-validation folds. A canonical correlation of 0.69 to 0.77 for the first
  mode at pentad +1 describes how well the fitted pair matches in-sample. The
  cross-validated correlation of the forecasts it produces is 0.26 to 0.31.
- The predictand EOFs depend on the observations alone, so they are identical for
  every model at a given lead (the notebook checks this). At pentad +1 the first three
  explain 18.9%, 8.5% and 5.4% of the variance, 33% together: most of the
  variance of a single pentad at 0.05° lies outside what three patterns describe.
- Loadings are in CPT's units and are scaled here so each map's largest absolute
  value is 1. Sign and shape carry meaning; magnitude does not.

## The forecasts, model by model

Each calibrated member gives a deterministic anomaly and three tercile
probabilities at every pixel; the ensemble averages them. A total is the 2000-2016
mean of the target plus the anomaly, set to zero where that falls below zero
(1,103, 881, 177, 119, 8 and 2 of 69,638 pixels for the CCA ensemble, by lead). The first view is
PyCPT's standard probabilistic map: the colour is the most likely category, darker
where its probability is higher.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof fcModel = selectControl("Model", modelChoices, "MME")
viewof fcMethod = selectControl("Calibration", ["CCA", "PCR"], "CCA")
viewof fcView = selectControl("Show", [["probability", "Most likely category and probability"], ["anomaly", "Forecast anomaly (mm)"], ["percent", "Forecast as % of normal"], ["total", "Forecast total"], ["observedCategory", "Observed category"], ["observedAnomaly", "Observed anomaly (mm)"], ["observed", "Observed total"]], "probability")
mmeForecastMaps(mme, geo, fcModel, fcMethod, fcView)
```
:::

### Against what happened

Each lead's target is checked against the observed total. The **hit rate** is the
share of area where the most likely category was the one observed; the grey
squares show what always forecasting the most widespread category would have
scored, a reference chosen with hindsight.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof scoreMethod = selectControl("Calibration", ["CCA", "PCR"], "CCA")
viewof scoreMetric = selectControl("Score", [["hit", "Hit rate"], ["rpss", "RPSS"], ["rmse", "RMSE"]], "hit")
mmeScoresByLead(mme, scoreMethod, scoreMetric)
```
:::

| Pentad +3 | 11-15 Nov 2023 | 39.8 | 34.1 | 45.9 | 49 / 33 / 18 | 74 / 15 | 41.9% | 49.1% (below) | 0.02 |
| Pentad +4 | 16-20 Nov 2023 | 41.7 | 31.2 | 48.1 | 64 / 23 / 12 | 71 / 16 | 49.3% | 64.5% (below) | 0.08 |

Sources: [issued-2023-10-31-forecasts.csv](../data/pentad-mme-2023/issued-2023-10-31-forecasts.csv), [issued-2023-10-31-observed.csv](../data/pentad-mme-2023/issued-2023-10-31-observed.csv).

The ensemble made below normal the most likely category over 53 to 89% of the
area. Below normal was the most widespread observed category at pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3 and pentad +4; at pentad +5 and pentad +6 it was near normal. The hit rate was within two points of the hindsight reference at pentad +5 and more than two points below it at pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3, pentad +4 and pentad +6. The RPSS against climatological odds was positive at pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3 and pentad +4 and negative at pentad +5 and pentad +6.
At pentad +1, pentad +2, pentad +3 and pentad +4 the area-mean forecast lay between the observed total and the 2000-2016 mean: on the dry side of normal, not as dry as observed.

One outcome per lead describes November 2023; it is not a measure of skill.

## The flexible forecast: probability of exceedance

A tercile map answers one question. The **flexible forecast** answers others: the
probability that the target's total exceeds a chosen amount at each pixel. It is
built with the conventions of PyCPT's `construct_flex_fcst` from the ensemble's
deterministic forecast and its prediction error variance, as a Student's t
distribution ([chapter 5](../learn/05-probabilistic-forecasts.ipynb) compares those
conventions with CPT's native ones).

The default threshold is each pixel's **climatological median**, so the map reads
as "chance of a wetter than median pentad" and 50% means no information. Choose
another percentile to ask about dry or wet extremes. **Click any pixel** to draw
its curves: the forecast distribution against the climatology, as probability of
exceedance and as density, with the observed total marked.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof flexLead = selectControl("Lead", leadChoices, "1")
viewof flexPercentile = selectControl("Threshold", [["10", "10th percentile (very dry)"], ["20", "20th percentile"], ["33", "33rd percentile"], ["50", "Median"], ["67", "67th percentile"], ["80", "80th percentile"], ["90", "90th percentile (very wet)"]], "50")
mmeFlexible(mme, geo, flexLead, flexPercentile)
```
:::

| Lead | Target | Mean chance of exceeding the median | Area with chance above 50% | Area observed above the median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pentad +1 | 1-5 Nov 2023 | 42% | 7% | 27% |
| Pentad +2 | 6-10 Nov 2023 | 44% | 13% | 23% |
| Pentad +3 | 11-15 Nov 2023 | 48% | 25% | 34% |
| Pentad +4 | 16-20 Nov 2023 | 47% | 23% | 21% |
| Pentad +5 | 21-25 Nov 2023 | 50% | 44% | 50% |
| Pentad +6 | 26-30 Nov 2023 | 50% | 52% | 51% |

: The CCA ensemble's flexible forecast, area-weighted. Source: [flexible-forecast.csv](../data/pentad-mme-2023/flexible-forecast.csv).

The forecast gave 7 to 52% of the area a better than even chance of a wetter than
median pentad; 21 to 51% of the area ended above its median.

The curves in the browser are computed from four stored fields per lead (forecast
centre and scale, climatological mean and scale). For pentad +1 the notebook builds
the same fields with `pycpt.construct_flex_fcst` itself and the exceedance
probabilities agree to within 0.001 percentage points. The degrees of freedom are
the number of training targets (300 to 305). Targets of the same year are not
independent samples, so the curves are probably too narrow; this page does not
measure by how much.

Like the tercile probabilities, these assume the t distribution describes the
forecast error well. The cross-validated RPSS above is this page's only test of
that.

## What this case shows, and what it does not

This is one issue date, five models, one set of fixed settings and one verifying
outcome per lead. It shows that for pentad rainfall over Indonesia in
October-December, a calibrated five-model ensemble does not clearly improve on
calibrated GEFSv12 alone (a correlation of 0.31, 0.31, 0.25, 0.22, 0.15 and 0.14 against
0.31, 0.30, 0.25, 0.24, 0.17 and 0.13: above it at pentad +1, pentad +2 and pentad +6, below it at pentad +4 and pentad +5), that its probabilities beat a no-model
forecast at every lead, and that the raw multi-model average correlates better
than any calibrated forecast here.

It does not show that these five models are the best set, or that equal weights
are the best weights: no other combination was tried. It does not show how other
settings behave. The observations are retrospective CHIRPS v3.0 Final data, not
what was available when the forecast was issued.

::: {.callout-tip title="Read it with the single-model case"}
The [single-model pentad case](pentad-leads-2023.qmd) follows GEFSv12 through every issue
date of October-December 2023. This page takes one of those issue dates and adds
four models.
:::
